antipodal_theorem.assumption: exact native metric G_* is antipodally radially injective
antipodal_theorem.statement: If an origin-centered sphere passes through a nonzero Cell3 lattice center p, its lattice intersection is exactly {p,-p}.
proof_steps: Write p=B_* n with n nonzero integer.
The sphere radius satisfies R^2=n^T G_* n.
The antipode -p=B_*(-n) has the same radius.
Any further q=B_* m on the sphere gives m^T G_* m=n^T G_* n.
Antipodal radial injectivity forces m=+/-n, hence q=+/-p.

circle_corollary.statement: For any origin-centered plane Pi containing p, C_(Pi,R)=S_R intersection Pi and C_(Pi,R) intersection Lambda_*={p,-p}.
circle_corollary.proof_core: A linear plane containing p also contains -p; the sphere theorem excludes every other lattice center.
